I am currently living in a small motor home during the week near where I am working but I travel every weekend to either my parents place 1.5hrs away or my boyfriends place 3hrs away. With the VERY small fridge and pantry space and constant traveling I have been finding it difficult to keep eating right and exercise regularly. I started crossfit 2x a week and I try to run on the weekends but everything is very unpredictable. So I was curious if anyone had any tips on how they stay in shape while traveling.
Big travelers: How do you work in eating right and exercising when your traveling?

I'm not sure where you are travelling but you should search for fitness parks or normal kids parks to do bodyweight stuff. I have traveled the world and also had good luck just walking into gyms, especially in foreign countries. Also, stop eating bad food, pantry space shouldn't be an excuse.

Pantry space shouldn't be and your right. But it is frustrating when I try to buy fresh foods that end of going bad because I leave for 3 days, it adds up. I've started buying less at a time and just try to run to the grocery store more often and that seems to have a helped some. I was hoping for some more ideas of easy to eat on the go foods (don't need to be in a cooler or are sticky/messy, etc.) that fill you u without bogging you down. It is also very hot where I am (norm is 90-100 F) and even hotter where my boyfriend is (100+F) so bananas or even just avocados sitting in the kitchen seem to ripen and go bad quickly.

My parents area would definitely have a fitness park somewhere and I haven't thought of looking for that, but I will now! However my boyfriends area is a VERY small town (maybe ~1,000 people?) and there are no gyms that I've found. There is one start-up yoga place but its closed on the weekends (when I am there).

Most schools have the basic equipment in their playgrounds...As far as food goes I would always have a few lbs. of rice, black beans, and lentils. Also a jug of protein powder. If you can grab fresh produce every other day you should be fine.

I make a travel pack of food when I travel. Usually contains beef jerky, nuts, Quest bars, etc. If it fits your macros , fit it in your pantry. Avoid food from your boyfriend/parents unless they understand your fitness situation and will accommodate your needs.

Regarding travel since it's only on weekends I wouldn't attempt finding a gym. Work out during the week when you're not traveling. If you want to do some cardio then run outside on the weekends. That's free.

I could see about making my own trail mix of different unsalted nuts and dried fruit that I like. I am not a fan of granola or protein bars, never seem to make me feel full or give me any extra energy.
